title: Coordinator, Digital Health (Ethiopia)
description: This role was posted on August 13, 2026. Please note that we will review applications on a rolling basis. About Last Mile Health Last Mile Health saves lives in the world's most remote communities. Our vision is a health worker within reach of everyone, everywhere. We partner with governments to recruit, train, equip, and integrate professional community health workers into national health systems, equipping them to deliver quality primary care in rural and remote communities. Founded in Liberia in 2007, we now operate programs in Ethiopia, Liberia, Sierra Leone, and Malawi. Our global offices are located in Accra, Ghana and in the United States. We are looking for mission-driven leaders to join us as we work to ensure no patient is out of reach. About The Ethiopia Team The Ethiopia team works in partnership with Ethiopia’s Ministry of Health to strengthen the country’s flagship Health Extension Program, a globally recognized model for delivering primary healthcare through more than 40,000 Health Extension Workers. Led by Abraham Zerihun, the team works to upskill the Health Extension Workers through blended learning that combines digital and in-person training. It also advances digital innovation through HEP Assist, an AI-powered clinical decision-support tool that helps Health Extension Workers provide evidence-based care at the point of service. The team's portfolio spans maternal, newborn, child health, nutrition, and non-communicable diseases, including hypertension, diabetes, eye care, and stroke prevention and management, while strengthening health systems through sustainable community health financing, resource mapping, and strategic planning to support long-term government leadership and program sustainability. The Role At Last Mile Health (LMH), we make bold commitments that inspire innovation. Do you have experience supporting digital health implementation, troubleshooting technology in the field, and working with frontline health workers to deploy and strengthen digital health solutions? If so, you may be the next Digital Health Coordinator at Last Mile Health. The Digital Health Coordinators will provide high level technical and implementation support for the deployment of LMH's digital health tools to Community Health Workers (CHWs) across Ethiopia, including Extension Essentials and HEP Assist AI. Reporting to the Director, Digital Health, Ethiopia, the Coordinators will support planning, coordination, and implementation of digital health activities, working closely with program teams, field teams, and users to ensure effective adoption and use of digital health solutions. Based in Addis Ababa, the role will provide hands-on support to digital health implementation and will travel to different regions as needed to support field deployment and training activities. The Coordinators will support workplan management, data collection and feedback processes, data analysis and dashboard development, application installation and troubleshooting, and the development and implementation of processes and procedures that strengthen digital health activities. The role will also provide remote technical support to users through phone, email, and relevant open source digital health communities. This advertisement is for two Digital Health Coordinator positions based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. This is a fixed-term position for 24–36 months, with the potential for renewal. The role is based onsite in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, and is open only to candidates who are currently located in and authorized to work in Ethiopia. What You'll Do Digital Health Solutions Implementation Coordination Coordinate with the Senior Digital Health Coordinators to ensure that the digital health initiatives are run successfully across all districts Work with the Director, Digital Health, Senior Manager of Digital Health, Ethiopia country office program team, the Global DH Manager, and other relevant internal LMH departments (MERL, HSS, etc.) to maintain and update deployment tasks in the implementation plan Roll out new Deployment Packages (latest apps and tools such as Extension Essentials and HEP Assist AI) to Health Extension Workers (HEWs) Support establishment of a digital health management processes and procedures for digital health activities Support Digital Health Training activities including the planning and deployment of a digital education platform for Health Extension Workers Coordinate, facilitate and participate in health worker and health systems leaders trainings across districts Support learners (health workers, Ministry of Health (MOH) and health system leaders) during training (including app installation on mobile device, etc.) and remotely after training Support LMH and MOH program managers/ Coordinators in creating user accounts for app access and maintain dashboards to track learners sync status and course performance Support data collection efforts for all digital health activities including data tracking, data

description: PATH current employees - please log in and apply Here PATH is a global nonprofit dedicated to achieving health equity. With more than 40 years of experience forging multisector partnerships and with expertise in science, economics, technology, advocacy, and dozens of other specialties, PATH develops and scales up innovative solutions to the world’s most pressing health challenges. PATH seeks a Regional Laboratory Officer for the United States Government (USG)-funded Reaching every at-risk community and household with malaria services (REACH Malaria) global project. REACH aims to provide implementation support services and technical assistance to countries to accelerate progress in comprehensive delivery of life-saving facility and community-based malaria services including malaria case management, prevention of malaria in pregnancy (MiP), seasonal malaria chemoprevention (SMC), maternal and child health services including immunization and nutrition, data collection and use for service delivery, and other malaria prevention interventions. Regional Laboratory Officer is responsible for supporting improvement of malaria laboratory diagnosis and quality assurance across REACH Malaria Project supported health facilities in the respective region. S/he is responsible for providing comprehensive technical support to health facilities, health care workers and communities to improve the quality of malaria laboratory diagnosis and quality assurance activities. S/he will be responsible for providing technical support including regular mentorship and supportive supervision and training to health facilities including health posts to improve the quality of malaria diagnosis in close collaboration with the regional, zonal, district and EQA center malaria and laboratory officers. The improved quality of malaria diagnosis will increase the quality of malaria case management services which is a life-saving intervention. Responsibilities: Provide regular mentorship to facility laboratory staff, regional and woreda malaria programs on malaria laboratory diagnosis and quality assurance Provide training to laboratory personnel and other HCWs on malaria laboratory diagnosis and quality assurance as well as integrated external quality assessment Assist development and/or review of support tools such mentorship checklist, job aids, laboratory SOPs to be provided to each health facility to support the improvement of malaria diagnosis practices Provide comprehensive support to health facility laboratories and health posts including the distribution of essential job aids, SOPs, guidelines and manuals as well as commodities to health facilities Conduct baseline assessment and follow up tailored support to each health center and health post on malaria laboratory diagnosis and quality assurance activities. Participate in the regular regional laboratory technical working group meetings Provide technical assistance for regional planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of malaria diagnosis and quality assurance activities.
